system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Mexico City, Mexico. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Mexico City itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Mexico City space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Colonia Juárez/Cuauhtémoc, San Miguel Chapultepec, Roma/Condesa, Polanco, San Rafael/Santa María la Ribera, Escandón, San Ángel/Coyoacán) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Mexico City spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Mexico City, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: kurimanzutto
galleries.note: The most internationally influential gallery in Mexico, founded 1999 by Mónica Manzutto and José Kuri with Gabriel Orozco; represents Abraham Cruzvillegas, Damián Ortega, Minerva Cuevas, Haegue Yang; spaces in New York.

galleries.name: Galería OMR
galleries.note: Founded 1983, a pillar of the Mexican scene; blue-chip and emerging programme, major fair presence, and driver of the Roma gallery district; also runs the LagoAlgo space.

galleries.name: LABOR
galleries.note: Research-driven programme of conceptual and politically engaged practices (Pedro Reyes, Adriana Lara, Iván Argote); consistent presence at Art Basel and Frieze.

galleries.name: Proyectos Monclova
galleries.note: Founded 2005; rigorous conceptual programme with artists such as Eduardo Terrazas, José León Cerrillo and Gabriel de la Mora; strong international fair circuit.

galleries.name: Galería Nordenhake
galleries.note: Stockholm/Berlin gallery whose 2019 Mexico City space brought a major European roster into dialogue with Latin American artists.

galleries.name: House of Gaga
galleries.note: Fernando Mesta's gallery, key to a generation of experimental artists; collaborations with Reena Spaulings and a Los Angeles outpost gave it outsized critical influence.

galleries.name: Travesía Cuatro
galleries.note: Madrid gallery with a permanent Mexico City house since 2017; shows Milena Muzquiz, José Dávila, Gonzalo Lebrija and other Spanish–Mexican crossovers.

galleries.name: Galería Hilario Galguera
galleries.note: Opened 2006 with Damien Hirst's first Mexican show; ambitious international programme in a landmark San Rafael mansion, plus a Madrid space.

galleries.name: Arróniz Arte Contemporáneo
galleries.note: Long-running gallery championing mid-career Mexican artists; regular at Zona Maco, ARCO and Latin American fairs.

galleries.name: PEANA
galleries.note: Monterrey-born gallery with a permanent Mexico City space; sharp young Latin American roster and a strong international fair profile.

galleries.name: Galería Agustina Ferreyra
galleries.note: Relocated from San Juan, Puerto Rico; influential Caribbean–Latin American programme with strong curatorial and fair visibility.

galleries.name: Guadalajara 90210
galleries.note: Idiosyncratic dealer-curator project that helped shape the taste of a younger Mexican scene; frequent presence at Material and international fairs.

galleries.name: Galería Curro
galleries.note: Guadalajara gallery with a Mexico City space; experimental, artist-led programme with consistent fair and institutional attention.

galleries.name: Anonymous Gallery
galleries.note: New York-founded gallery now anchored in Mexico City; cross-border programme of emerging and mid-career artists with a lively public events schedule.

galleries.name: Galería RGR
galleries.note: Specialist in kinetic, op and geometric abstraction alongside contemporary positions; large architecturally notable space and steady fair presence.

galleries.name: Galería Karen Huber
galleries.note: Focused on contemporary painting; discovered and internationalised several young Mexican painters now in institutional collections.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: Chicago/Paris gallery whose Mexico City space brought a leading roster of African-diaspora artists into permanent dialogue with the local scene.

galleries.name: Machete Galería
galleries.note: Young gallery with an irreverent programme of emerging Mexican artists; active at Material and Zona Maco.

galleries.name: Galería Mascota
galleries.note: Emerging-focused gallery known for adventurous painting and sculpture shows and an energetic international fair strategy.

galleries.name: Lodos
galleries.note: Small but critically respected gallery that launched several artists now shown internationally; a fixture of Mexico City art week.

galleries.name: Pequod Co.
galleries.note: Artist-founded gallery representing a strong cohort of young Mexican painters and sculptors; regular at Material and Zona Maco.

galleries.name: Galería de Arte Mexicano (GAM)
galleries.note: Founded 1935, the oldest gallery in Mexico; historic home of the muralists and still an active contemporary and modern programme.

galleries.name: Galería López Quiroga
galleries.note: Authoritative modern and contemporary dealer (Francisco Toledo, Vicente Rojo, Manuel Álvarez Bravo estate); a benchmark for the Mexican market.

galleries.name: Parque Galería
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a curatorially minded programme of Mexican and Latin American artists and consistent fair participation.

galleries.name: Yautepec Gallery
galleries.note: Founded by the organisers of Material Art Fair's predecessor scene; long-standing champion of emerging Mexican and international artists.

galleries.name: Proyecto Paralelo
galleries.note: Research- and archive-oriented gallery with strong conceptual and documentary programming.

galleries.name: Terreno Baldío Arte
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery known for socially engaged and site-responsive projects by mid-career Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Galería Enrique Guerrero
galleries.note: Founded 1998; established contemporary programme of Mexican and Latin American artists with long fair history.

galleries.name: Galería Nina Menocal
galleries.note: Pioneer of the Roma gallery scene from 1990 and key promoter of Cuban artists in Mexico.

galleries.name: Galería Juan Martín
galleries.note: Founded 1961; historic space for the Ruptura generation, still showing contemporary Mexican art.

galleries.name: Patricia Conde Galería
galleries.note: Mexico's leading photography gallery, representing classic and contemporary Mexican photographers.

galleries.name: Almanaque Fotográfica
galleries.note: Contemporary photography gallery and publishing project that has renewed critical interest in the medium in Mexico.

galleries.name: MAIA Contemporary
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with an international emerging roster and steady presence at Mexican and European fairs.

galleries.name: Saenger Galería
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a Latin American and international programme and regular Zona Maco participation.

galleries.name: Galería Ethra
galleries.note: Long-running gallery showing established and mid-career Mexican artists across painting, sculpture and photography.

galleries.name: Ginocchio Galería
galleries.note: Contemporary Latin American programme with a strong collector base and consistent fair presence.

galleries.name: Galería Óscar Román
galleries.note: Established Polanco gallery showing contemporary Mexican painting and sculpture since the 1990s.

galleries.name: Galería Alberto Misrachi
galleries.note: Heir to one of Mexico City's oldest dealer families; modern Mexican masters alongside contemporary work.

galleries.name: Fifty24MX Gallery
galleries.note: Mexican outpost of the Upper Playground/FIFTY24 network; central to street-art-derived and urban contemporary practices in the city.

galleries.name: Galería Hydra
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a young experimental programme and active participation in Mexico City art week.

galleries.name: Neter
galleries.note: Gallery and cultural platform pairing contemporary art with design and publishing projects.

galleries.name: EDS Galería
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery representing Mexican and international artists, a regular at Zona Maco.

galleries.name: Marso
galleries.note: Foundation and exhibition space in a Juárez townhouse, known for residencies and ambitious project-based shows.

galleries.name: Salón Silicón
galleries.note: Feminist and queer-focused gallery/project space that has become a reference point for younger critical practices in Mexico City.

galleries.name: Biquini Wax EPS
galleries.note: Artist-run collective and house space; one of the most cited independent platforms of the last decade, with international curatorial attention.

galleries.name: Cráter Invertido
galleries.note: Artist collective, printing press and social space; participant in documenta and biennials, emblematic of Mexico City's self-organised scene.

galleries.name: Ladrón Galería
galleries.note: Independent gallery/project space with a fast-moving programme of emerging artists and off-circuit exhibitions.

galleries.name: Tlaxcala3
galleries.note: Artist-run space in a Roma apartment building known for concise, experimental shows by young artists.

galleries.name: SOMA
galleries.note: Artist-led educational and exhibition platform whose public programme, SOMA Summer and Miércoles de SOMA talks shaped a whole generation.

galleries.name: Fundación Casa Wabi – Sabino
galleries.note: Mexico City home of Bosco Sodi's foundation, in an Alberto Kalach building; exhibitions, residencies and community programmes.

galleries.name: LagoAlgo
galleries.note: Free cultural space run by Galería OMR in a modernist lakeside pavilion, staging large-scale contemporary exhibitions for a broad public.

galleries.name: Fundación Alumnos47
galleries.note: Foundation with an art library, public programmes and commissions supporting critical contemporary practice and pedagogy.

galleries.name: Casa Maauad
galleries.note: International residency and exhibition house that has hosted a wide network of artists working in Mexico City.

galleries.name: Casa Gallina
galleries.note: inSite's neighbourhood-based art initiative in Santa María la Ribera, linking artists with community and public programmes.

galleries.name: Casa Vecina
galleries.note: Downtown cultural space with contemporary exhibitions, residencies and community projects in the historic centre.

galleries.name: Border
galleries.note: Independent art space and residency focused on critical, socially engaged and pedagogical projects.

galleries.name: Galería Metropolitana (UAM)
galleries.note: Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana's public gallery, a long-standing venue for experimental and politically engaged exhibitions.

galleries.name: Casa del Lago UNAM
galleries.note: UNAM's historic cultural centre in Chapultepec with a consistently strong contemporary art, sound and performance programme.

galleries.name: Galería José María Velasco
galleries.note: Public gallery of the national fine arts institute with a community-rooted, experimental contemporary programme.

galleries.name: AGO Projects
galleries.note: Leading collectible design gallery commissioning Latin American designers and artists; major presence at Design Miami and art week.

galleries.name: MASA Galería
galleries.note: Nomadic collectible-design gallery whose exhibitions in landmark Mexican buildings blur art, craft and architecture.

galleries.name: Casa Lamm
galleries.note: Cultural centre in a Roma mansion whose galleries have shown modern and contemporary Mexican art since 1993.

galleries.name: Aeromoto
galleries.note: Public art-book library and artist-run platform; a meeting point for the city's independent publishing and exhibition scene.
